_source: docs/04 §11.2's definition file. ✅ CANON (A9): 'You can only ever find 1 Legendary per class - They are also named characters - IE Natsuna(the shaman) or something.'
_notes: docs/04 §11.2's definition file, hand-authored, no procedural fields.

docs/03 §5.6: 'The other 8 Legendary names — ❓ OPEN, naming pending. Use placeholders `Legendary (Warrior) — name pending`. DO NOT INVENT NAMES.' So `display_name` is null on eight of the nine files and the loader renders that placeholder. Everything that is NOT a name is authored, because it survives the naming pass unchanged.

docs/04 §11.2 on `starting_morale`: 'Optional override only. Default is null, meaning the computed baseline per docs/05 §4/§7.5 — not a fixed 75.' Null on all nine: canon shows Natsuna at 87 morale in an example ROSTER, which is a snapshot of a played game rather than an arrival value (docs/15 BL-57).

`subscribed_tags` is docs/04 §11.3's direct expression of ✅ CANON A11 — 'legendary raiders will not be bothered by many things easily'. Only the tags in this character's own backstory reach them; every other morale event is ignored outright. Two bullets each, so eight of the ten trigger families cannot touch them.

`quirk` is named here and its mechanics belong to docs/07, which has not specced them — so the quirk is inert until it does (docs/15 BL-58). A named-but-inert gift is honest; an invented one would have to be balanced twice.
